title: Loom playback: probe launchpad and request stitch notes
content:
TL;DR: This note bundles ~25 field requests from enterprise and mid-market customers encountered between Feb 15–Mar 18, 2026. Themes: unpredictable tail latency under mixed short/long sequences, KV-cache misses causing regressed token cost, rollout UX confusion when model variants are used as fallbacks, and a set of low-effort UX/ops patches that could materially reduce support volume. Below is a prioritized probe launchplan + suggested quick fixes and hypotheses to validate in a 3-week spike.

Context and scope:
- Source signals: weekly CS triage channel, three customer architecture reviews (two banking, one healthtech), and runtime error logs correlated with customer incident reports.
- Not representative of all customers; weighted to teams using Dedicated pools with hybrid short-lived chat + long-context summarization workloads.

Synthesis highlights (narrative):
1) Latency variance: Customers report 95th/99th latencies spiking when interactive chat and large-batch summarization jobs share the same shard. Several callouts about degraded UX during peak ingest windows.
2) Caching incongruence: Engineers expect prefix/KV caching to kick in on repeated system prompts, but observed cache miss patterns and token re-encoding add both cost and latency. Customers see sudden bill jumps when their chatbots switch to new 'session IDs'.
3) Fallback opacity: When we route to cheaper model variants during capacity pressure, customers see semantic drift but no clear UI signal. They assume a silent failure.
4) Tool-calling / function-calls: A few customers reported function call truncation on long contexts — appears to be a windowing + JSON-emit edge case.

Representative customer quotes (as reported):
- "We see our interactive responses go from 120ms to >1.8s during our nightly batch — our UX metrics plummet." — fintech PM
- "Cache seems to miss whenever our session ID rotates on our side. Are you deduping prefix prompts?" — eCommerce infra lead
- "The model changed subtly overnight — our tests started failing and we had no clue which variant served." — large enterprise SRE

Concrete asks and proposed probes (prioritized):
A — Latency segregation probe (high impact, mid effort)
- Hypothesis: Mixed workload on same pool causes kernel choice thrashing and queuing.
- Probe: Create 2 pilot pools with identical models but workload-tag-based routing: pool-A (short 1–2 token regen; low burst), pool-B (long-context summarization). Measure token-per-second and 95/99 latencies for 2 weeks.
- Success metric: 95th latency reduction >40% for short-paths; reduced SLO breaches.
- Suggested tickets: ENG-4231 (create workload-tag router), SRE-551 (trace heatmaps).

B — KV-cache stability test (high impact, low effort)
- Hypothesis: Session-bound cache keys are too brittle; client-side session rotation invalidates caches causing re-encodes.
- Probe: Add a server-side optional 'session-alias' header allowing stable cache keying for 30m windows. Enable for 3 pilot customers and measure cache hit rates and token costs.
- Quickfix: Document recommended session key patterns in SDKs + add warning in console when cache hit rate < X%.

C — Fallback transparency UX (mid impact, low effort)
- Problem: silent routing to variant models causes trust issues.
- Proposal: Add a response header + console flag that indicates model_variant and fallback_reason. Default to off for privacy but opt-in for enterprise.
- Quick customer benefit: reduces support tickets where customers ask "which model did you run?"

D — Function-calls windowing regression test (mid impact, mid effort)
- Reproduce with two customers who reported truncation. Build synthetic harness that feeds nested JSON calls and 10–30k token contexts and watch function-call tokens emitted.
- Ticket: QA-702 (regression harness)

Low-effort patches (week 1 items):
- Add console quicknote "cache hit rate" on route pages and warn if <30% (owner: product-console).
- Small docs patch: "session ID and cache best practices" in SDK quickstarts with code snippets for stable session aliasing (owner: dev-x).
- Default tweak: When routing to cheaper fallback, keep original model name in logs for 48 hrs and include delta summary (cheap vs fast) in console change logs (owner: product-hosted-api).
- Support playbook: one-pager for CS to triage latency calls: list of checks (pool-tag, cache-hit, recent rollouts).

Impact / effort table (informal):
- KV-cache alias header: low effort, high ROI in token cost reduction for 3 large customers.
- Fallback transparency header: very low effort, defuses many trust tickets.
- Latency segregation pilot: mid effort (infra changes), high ROI if it restores 95th latency.
- Function-call regression harness: mid effort, required to pin subtle truncation bugs.

Open questions & risks (notes-to-self):
- Will aliasing session keys create security/PII concerns? Need legal sign-off on header semantics.
- Can workload-tag routing be achieved purely in control plane or does it need runtime kernel selection flags? (Ping infra/serving-runtime)
- If we surface fallback variant by default, are there customers that will find this a data-exposure issue?

Next steps (who/when):
- Week 0 (this week): Share with ENG-servicing + Product-hosted-api for feasibility check (owner: Ayesha).
- Week 1: Implement console cache-hit indicator + docs patch (owners: Claire + DevX).
- Week 1–3: Spin up KV-cache alias pilot for 3 customers (Samir to lead outreach; SRE instrumentation ticket SRE-551).
- Week 2–4: Start workload-segmentation pilot planning with serving-runtime (Diego to coordinate).

Appendix (raw snippets & testing notes):
- Example SDK pattern for session-alias header (notes):
  
  // pseudo-code
  sessionAlias = hash(userId + conversationId)
  client.send({ prompt: "<system>", headers: { "x-session-alias": sessionAlias } })

- Quick log line examples to look for: "cacheHit=false sessionAlias=null model_variant=redwood-lite fallback=cost"

Unresolved action items:
- Legal review on header semantics (Ayesha)
- Feasibility runbook for workload-tag router (Diego)
- Pilot customer signoff list (Samir + CS AE team)

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally lightweight — aim for a 1-pager customer-facing executive summary if pilots show promise. If any of the quickfixes land, track reduction in CS tickets for 30 days and report back.

End of note.

-- A.P.
summary: Actionable synthesis of Feb–Mar customer feedback: latency segregation, KV-cache brittleness, opaque fallback behavior. Probes suggested: workload-tag routing, session-alias header pilot, fallback transparency header, function-call regression harness. Quick patches for console and docs to reduce support load.
